source.title: Training Machine Learning Models on Human Spatio-temporal Mobility Data: An Experimental Study [Experiment Paper]
source.authors: Yue-Yang Liu; Lance Kennedy; Ruochen Kong; Joon-Seok Kim; Andreas Züfle

record.tranche_reason: Tests how batch size affects held-out prediction in human mobility data, extending batch-size generalization findings to a new domain and task.
record.gate_note: The paper does not test arbitrary-label memorization or the claim's other mapped factors. Batch-size experiments report GEO-BLEU by model, dataset, and batch size; the text also says accuracy remained largely unchanged across batch settings. Epoch budget is not stated.
record.test_reason: The study varies training batch size and measures held-out trajectory prediction quality, extending the batch-size question in V5 to human mobility. It tests the directional performance relationship, but does not establish V5's fixed-epoch condition.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly accurate for the batch-size finding: the authors conclude that smaller batches improve GEO-BLEU at increased training time, while large batches train faster but can require over 60 GB of memory. They also explicitly report largely unchanged accuracy. Their broader conclusions emphasize historical fusion, temporal context, and sampling; semantic user embeddings can reduce performance.
record.recipe_differences: Varying batch size in human mobility trajectory prediction with Transformer and LSTM models; epoch budget is not stated, and the study does not test arbitrary-label memorization.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size changes GEO-BLEU; the direction is broadly consistent across datasets and architectures, with a small NYC LSTM uptick at batch size 256 relative to 64. GEO-BLEU is more sensitive than accuracy to subtle differences.
record.problems: The study does not state a fixed epoch budget for the batch-size comparison. It uses mobility prediction and GEO-BLEU, not the generalization-gap measures or tasks in the claim versions; no uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant batch-size performance rows omitted. Table 3 sampling-strategy comparisons and Table 4 feature/fusion comparisons do not test a listed claim version.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label held-out performance.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Optimizer comparisons and tuning budgets; using Adam alone does not test V4.
Whether epochs were held fixed; image-classification and language-model workloads; recovery through longer training, learning-rate scaling, warmup, normalization, or regularization changes.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance and its correlation with generalization gaps.
Influence-based identification and removal of memorized examples.

missing.what: Batch-size accuracy result: accuracy remained largely unchanged across settings. Record the qualitative result as absent, with model attribution limited to what Section 5.3.2 establishes; numerical values are not supplied.

Additional batch-size sweeps within Table 4's extended-temporal, user-semantic, and Fusion Predictor configurations. These are relevant batch comparisons even though rows_left_out dismisses feature/fusion comparisons. For example, fusion Transformer scores fall from 0.3547 to 0.2840 in NYC and 0.2675 to 0.2255 in Tokyo between batches 4 and 512; fusion LSTM scores also decline overall.
missing.locator: Table 4, compare batch sizes within each configuration and dataset

record.verdict_notes: All extracted baseline GEO-BLEU values match Table 4. No uncertainty estimates or controlled epoch counts are reported, so the results cannot establish a fixed-epoch causal penalty or statistical significance. The study is not an original source for V5.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural labels.
Width sweep beyond interpolation and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image models.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizers and tuning.
Fixed epoch budget is not stated; tested human-mobility prediction rather than image classification or language modeling.
Magnitude-aware sharpness or other measures tracking the training-test gap.

relationships.condition: Transformer, NYC and Tokyo, baseline inputs, batches 16–512 versus 4; epoch budget unreported.
relationships.reason: R1–R10 show lower held-out GEO-BLEU at every larger batch: NYC falls from 0.3341 to 0.2315 and Tokyo from 0.2367 to 0.1417. This supports the directional component only.
relationships.display_finding: Every larger Transformer batch scored below batch 4 in both New York City and Tokyo, although equal epoch budgets were unverified.

source_check.reason: R1–R10 confirm lower GEO-BLEU at every larger batch in both cities. Support is directional; the fixed-epoch condition remains untested.
